## 1. The law, theorem and distinction from the previous conditional result

Fix a connected compact boundaryless smooth manifold X, a smooth Riemannian
metric g, and a fixed dimension d >= 1. Write V = vol_g(X). Choose deterministic
real functions phi_j in C-infinity(X), j >= 1, such that their real linear span
is dense in the usual C-infinity topology. Choose strictly positive a_j with

    A_q = sum_j a_j ||phi_j||_Cq < infinity, for every integer q >= 0.       (1)

The norms can be the increasing norms sum_{h<=q} sup_X |nabla^h f|_g;
coordinate norms from a finite atlas are equivalent. Let Z_j be independent
standard real Gaussians and define the actual law by

    F = sum_j a_j Z_j phi_j.                                             (2)

Neither stationarity, constant variance, isotropy, parity, a flat metric, nor
a distinguished global frame is required. The independent Gaussian law and
the full dense support are substantive hypotheses. The covariance is the
actual smooth kernel K(p,q) = sum_j a_j^2 phi_j(p) phi_j(q).

law_construction_literal_slice.literal_text:
For m in Z^d put

    p_m=2pi m/L,
    Z_L=sum_m exp(-|p_m|^2/2),
    w_m=exp(-|p_m|^2/2)/Z_L.                                     (3)

All sums are over the ENTIRE lattice. Z_L is finite and strictly
positive and every w_m>0. Factorization of nonnegative sums gives

    Z_L=z_L^d,
    z_L=sum_{k in Z} exp(-(2pi k/L)^2/2).                          (4)

Thus the spectral probability vector with masses w_m has exactly
ORIGINAL's independent symmetric coordinates Q_i of Section2. The
notation p_m here separates wave numbers from probability masses;
it does not change ORIGINAL's q_m=2pi m/L convention.

Choose a set H containing one member of every nonzero pair {m,-m}.
Let Z_0 and (X_m,Y_m)_{m in H} be mutually independent standard real
Gaussians. Define the ACTUAL field

    F_L(x)=sqrt(w_0)Z_0
        +sum_{m in H} sqrt(2w_m)
              [X_m cos(p_m.x)+Y_m sin(p_m.x)].                    (5)

This retains the random spatially constant zero mode. There is no
additional L^(-d/2) basis normalization or samplewise mean removal.
The deterministic smooth functions in(5) are1 and the literal sine/
cosine functions, with strictly positive coefficients sqrt(w_0) and
sqrt(2w_m). Each fixed Cq norm is bounded by C_q(1+|p_m|)^q.

For every integer q>=0,

    sum_{m in H} sqrt(2w_m)(1+|p_m|)^q < infinity.                 (6)

For a direct proof, sqrt(w_m) is a fixed positive multiple of
exp(-|2pi m/L|^2/4). Group lattice points by integer shells in |m|.
The number in the k-th shell is at most C_d(1+k)^d. Its polynomial
factor times exp(-c_L k^2) is summable, since for all sufficiently
large k any prescribed polynomial is at most exp(c_L k^2/2), and
sum exp(-c_L k^2/2) is bounded by a geometric tail. The finitely
many smaller k do not matter. Constants depend on this fixed L,d.

The real span is dense in C-infinity(X). For a smooth periodic f,
repeated integration by parts makes its Fourier coefficients decay
faster than any polynomial in |m|. For each q choose enough integrations
so the derivative Fourier coefficients are absolutely summable.
Finite symmetric partial sums converge in Cq, and the same sequence
converges in every Cq. Their real form is a combination of the1,
sine and cosine functions in(5). This proves the required smooth
density, not merely L2 completeness.

One can see smooth convergence of(5) directly as well. For each q,
the expectation of the sum of Cq bounds with |X_m|,|Y_m| is finite
by(6), hence the sum is finite almost surely. Countably intersect
over q. The derivative series then converge absolutely and uniformly,
giving an actual smooth Borel field. Minkowski gives all finite
positive moments of its smooth norms. This is the same actual series
construction admitted by GAD, with no truncation used as a source law.
